claims.text: Introducing a specific type of precipitate can concurrently improve strength and ductility in certain alloys.
The initial material is aluminum alloy 2024 in the T6 condition.
The proposed intervention is aging at 160°C for 12 hours.
Aging aluminum alloy 2024-T6 at 160°C for 12 hours will form a uniform distribution of coherent Al3Sc precipitates.
The aging treatment is conducted in an inert atmosphere.
Using an inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during aging.
The structural mediator is a population of coherent Al3Sc precipitates.
Coherent Al3Sc precipitates impede dislocation movement.
A uniform precipitate distribution maintains a high level of ductility.
The treatment will increase yield strength by 20% relative to the baseline.
The treatment will increase elongation at break by 15% relative to the baseline.
Concurrent strength–ductility improvement occurs only within a narrow range of precipitate sizes and distributions.
The outcome depends on the initial microstructure, precise aging conditions, precipitate size, and precipitate distribution.
The baseline is aluminum alloy 2024 in the T6 condition without aging treatment.

contradictions.description: The initial and baseline material is described as T6, a condition that conventionally includes artificial aging, while the baseline is also described as being 'without aging treatment.' It is unclear whether the intervention is an additional aging step or whether the baseline is actually unaged.
